A systematic review and thematic synthesis exploring how a previous experience of physical activity influences engagement with cardiac rehabilitation
sources.authors: McHale S, Astin F, Neubeck L, Dawkes S, Hanson CL.

sources.title: The impact of breast cancer on fears of exercise and exercise identity
sources.authors: Murray J, Perry R, Pontifex E, Selva-Nayagam S, Bezak E, Bennett H.

sources.title: Women's exercise identity increases after a 16-week exercise RCT and is linked to behavior maintenance at follow-up
sources.authors: Gillman AS, Stevens CJ, Bryan AD.

findings.finding: Exercise identity is one of the key factors influencing adherence behavior.
findings.quote: Results show that three factors were particularly important in influencing adherence behavior: (i) exercise identity, (ii) support and (iii) perceived benefits of attending.

findings.finding: Self-perceptions of an exercise identity help influence engagement in physical activity.
findings.quote: For previously active individuals, communication factors, self-perceptions of an exercise identity and experience of cardiac rehabilitation influence engagement in physical activity during cardiac rehabilitation.

findings.finding: Participation in a supervised exercise intervention can increase women's exercise identity.
findings.quote: On average, participants experienced a statistically significant change in exercise identity over the course of the intervention, t (128) = 7.94, p p = .91.

findings.finding: Greater change in exercise identity is associated with higher levels of subsequent exercise behavior.
findings.quote: As expected, greater change in exercise identity was associated with higher levels of exercise behavior at 6-months post-intervention follow-up

principle: Developing an exercise identity through sustained participation and support helps maintain long-term physical activity habits.
for_the_teacher: Use language that reinforces the learner's self-perception as a dancer to build their exercise and movement identity.
